claim: The ref lane can lose a durable transaction from its in-memory view and then permanently hide that transaction behind a snapshot, making the defect data-loss class.

The ref-lane fix makes the interval between durable ref-log publication and runtime installation allocation-free at all three post-durable install sites, enforced by `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` and reinforced with an apply-pending poison marker.

The relink receiver protocol is publish → confirm → promote: the receiver durably publishes its `+1`, performs one read-only interserver query proving the sender still has the exact committed manifest binding, and promotes only after that proof succeeds.

The publish-confirm and ref-lane changes do not modify GC folding, journal codecs, snapshot formats, sweeps, orphan protection, or anomaly/suppression semantics; Part A changes only how a committed transaction is installed.

The operative CAS gtest gate is `build/src/unit_tests_dbms --gtest_filter='Ca*:CA*:ContentAddressed*:CountingBackendShape*:RefSnapshotCodec*:RefTableCacheEviction*:RefWriter*:*CasBackendContract*'`; the shorter `Cas*:CA*` filter omits parameterized `*/CasBackendContract` suites.
CAS code uses `LOGICAL_ERROR` only for genuine programming invariants and uses `CORRUPTED_DATA`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, or `ABORTED` for the corresponding existing CAS error classes.
CAS blob in-degree is a SET of source edges with last-wins semantics per key, not a counter; an unmatched removal is a per-key no-op and cannot remove a sibling manifest edge for the same blob.

`commitRefChunk` builds and applies a COW candidate before the ref-log PUT, so allocation failures occur before durability; the candidate is not materialized before the PUT because its shared COW base would force an O(n) rebuild per chunk.

`RefTableState::swap(RefTableState & other) noexcept` is the sanctioned post-durable installation operation, and member-wise swaps keep destruction of the old state outside the allocation-denied install region.

The `PostDurableInstall` `CarvePhaseForTest` hook fires after `putIfAbsentControlled` returns `Committed` and before the candidate is installed, providing the test seam for post-durable failure injection.
The unresolved ref-log wedge is preconstructed before the PUT so its exact `{id, key, bytes}` can be moved into runtime state without allocation after an ambiguous outcome.

Wedge resolution is a post-durable install: it must install the decoded transaction exactly once by noexcept swap, clear the wedge in the deny region, and swallow a later `materializeCommitted` failure so the same transaction is not re-applied.

`RefApplyState` has `Clean`, `ApplyPending`, and `Poisoned` states; a successful commit, conclusive PUT failure, definite failure, or absent wedge resolution clears `ApplyPending`, while a post-durable install failure transitions to `Poisoned`, which later successful flushes must never clear.
`precommitAdd` may introduce an unowned `ManifestId` only when the same transaction freshly staged it, except that the idempotent already-committed-to-this-exact-ref path remains legal.

The shipped TLA+ confirm model permits a dangle when one durable journal record is omitted from a paginated observation: `_sab_holeylist` violates the dangle property, and `_main` with `MaxHoles = 0` proves only that the confirm protocol adds no new dangle path under a completeness assumption.

`confirmExactRef` answers whether `ref_name` in a namespace still names exactly `manifest_ref` in the writer's committed view, performs zero object-store I/O, and returns `Unknown` for cold, evicted, or recovering tables instead of recovering them.

`confirmExactRef` must try-lock `state_mutex` while holding the ref queue mutex; failure to acquire it is treated as `Unknown` so confirmation never blocks pool-wide append admission behind recovery I/O.
A `Yes` from `confirmExactRef` excludes stale-cache, pending, in-flight, wedge, poison, and fence ambiguity but does not prove that the recovered runtime replayed every durable journal record.
`ownsNamespace` is required for confirm routing because a pool UUID is shared across server roots and cannot by itself select the answering mount.

The exchange-level gate-0 resolver returns `Unknown` for zero or multiple namespace matches and otherwise requires the named part to be `Active` or `Outdated` on the matched instance's disk, including the same-name `MOVE ... TO DISK` case.

The confirm fence rule is evaluated last, so gate-0 `No`, gate-1 `No`, and every `Unknown` reach the same caller outcome; future code must not treat `No` as authoritative without hoisting the fence rule.
`PreparedPartWrite` makes the receiver's durable `+1` and deferred promote an owned state: callers must explicitly `promote` or `abort`, because destruction of the handle alone is not cleanup.

Move assignment for `PreparedPartWrite` is deleted because overwriting a handle that still owes a terminal action may require a fallible `abandon`, which move assignment cannot report without dropping cleanup ownership.
Publish-confirm uses protocol version 11 with `content_addressed_confirm` as the confirm action parameter and `content_addressed_source_token` as the relink-offer response cookie.

The sender mints the source token from the same resolution that obtains the manifest bytes; a second lookup could allow a repoint between offer and mint and authorize a token for a manifest whose entries were not adopted.

The confirm wire is binary and fail-closed: only `yes` authorizes, while `No`, `Unknown`, and an absent cookie are all treated as unproven; old receivers ignore the unknown cookie and old senders offer relink without a token.

`prepareAdoptFromManifest` returns `Prepared` or `MechanismFallbackAllowed`; a confirm failure is not mechanism fallback, so the receiver must abort and throw a retry-later `NETWORK_ERROR` rather than byte-fetching on an unproven source.

Relink promotion has three outcomes: `Committed`, `MechanismFallbackAllowed` only when non-commit is proven, and `Unresolved` when promotion may have committed; `Unresolved` requires retrying the whole fetch rather than sequential byte fallback.

`allow_ca_relink` is an explicit capability separate from `try_zero_copy`; every byte-fallback re-request passes `allow_ca_relink=false` to prevent persistent mechanism failure from recursively relinking.

Detached relink targets are passed as disk-relative part paths so the CAS side derives the namespace and ref itself; `detached/<name>` is folded into routing, while a non-live-part target throws instead of falling back to bytes at the wrong location.

A flat blob count cannot prove that relink ran because a byte fetch onto a content-addressed disk writes identical content and deduplicates; positive proof must use the receiver log line `Relink of part

… finished (no bytes transferred).`.
S42 covers query-thread allocation faults only; thread-creation allocation faults are a separate class deferred to S43 because the ref append lane runs on the caller's thread.
S42's detailed fsck oracle must fail closed when `stale_edge` is absent, because `stale_edge` is detail-mode-only and a missing key can indicate a binary that predates the invariant.

`NoAttemptSent` means both pre-attempt gates rejected before `backend->putIfAbsent`; therefore `commitRefChunk` must not install a wedge, while a fence lost after an attempt (`FenceLostMidWay`) must still wedge.

`CasUnresolvedReason::NoAttemptSent` distinguishes a provably unwritten key from an ambiguous unresolved PUT, and `CasRefAppendPreAttemptRefused` preserves observability after the no-wedge behavior removes the wedge as evidence.

A diagnostic process opening a live CA pool through `Pool::mountWritable` can fail ownership claiming because the running server legitimately owns the server root; the failure is indistinguishable from a real mount-ownership defect unless the tool's contract is made explicit.
`fsck` can read `gc/state` and then stream source-edge runs after a snap-prune retires that generation, producing `CORRUPTED_DATA` on an otherwise healthy pool.

Thread-allocation fault injection through `cannot_allocate_thread_fault_injection_probability` targets background GC scheduling, mount-lease renewal, self-remount, and snapshot publication; lease fencing during the fault is fail-closed behavior, but recovery after disarm must be verified.

The stage-1 fan-out originally scheduled a task before appending its handle to an unreserved tracking vector, so a tracking allocation failure could leave a runnable task untracked and later dereferencing destroyed transaction or result-slot storage.

The stage-1 ref-lane leader originally published `leader_active = true` before allocating its first responsibility entry, so an allocation exception could strand the leadership baton and block later appends indefinitely.
The `DispatchThrowStillDrains` test was racy because it could cancel the first scheduled task before task entry; a latch must prove that already-running work is drained before dispatch unwinds.
Stage 1 parallelizes blobs within each part, while part publication remains a serial loop; comments claiming Task 5 parallelizes cross-part publication are false for the as-built stage.

The stage-1 composition review found no Pool/ledger/dispatcher/semaphore lock cycle; the dispatcher releases its mutex before invoking the sink, and condemned-local admission ends before event and metadata work.

CAS removal classification and chunking share the same op-inspection discriminator: production `RemoveNamespace` is `WholeShard`-scoped and singleton-carved, while normal chunks split before exceeding the operation cap.
Recovery rejects raw or compressed ref-log bodies over the configured cap with `CORRUPTED_DATA`; corruption is not classified as transient and is rethrown instead of triggering a relist.
Current-build `set_published_at` ref-log encode, decode, and apply preserve the same ref name, expected manifest, and timestamp.

The 64 MiB CAS upload value is a chosen default per-task memory budget, not a blob-body size cap; blob bodies are uncapped and an overweight body is admitted exclusively using its actual header-plus-source weight.

The final recovery memory guards use decoded transaction footprints and require both an upper bound near one transaction and a lower bound at least as large as the largest actual transaction, including an independent ledger recovery test.
`sealed_from` is paired with `newest_snapshot_id`: recovery seals install both values, while later ordinary or removed snapshots adopt a null `sealed_from` and clear the predecessor seal binding.
The removed snapshot/ref-log field `pl` is explicitly rejected in both former wire locations, including negative decoding tests, rather than silently ignored.
The wide S41 CA INSERT fell from 58.41 seconds before stage 1 to 30.26 seconds after stage 1, a 48% reduction and 1.93x speedup; plain S3 remained 19.44 versus 19.05 seconds.
The S41 stage-1 workload produced 500 CA parts and 3.53 GiB of logical bytes in both runs, while the CA-vs-plain factor fell from 3.0x to 1.59x.
The wide S41 profile averaged approximately 80 blob upload fan-out tasks per part (`40,150 / 500`), explaining why intra-part fan-out exceeded the narrow-case estimate of roughly two blobs per part.
On the CA INSERT, stage 1 reduced the top thread's Real-sample share from 72.3% to 14.5%, increased distinct Real-trace threads from 3 to 33, and increased CPU-busy/wall from 0.375 to 1.075.
The CA write path remained S3-network-bound at about 87% of Real wall time after stage 1; stage 1 overlapped that network work without removing it, while the HEAD-before-PUT gate remained about 12%.
For the 500-part S41 CA leg, PUTs stayed at 119,432, while HEADs fell from 134,400 to 105,140 and GETs from 54,360 to 42,656 after stage 1.
`CasRefBatchFlushes = CasRefBatchedMutations = 1000` over 500 S41 parts, so the average ref-ledger batch size remained 1.0; stage 1 intentionally did not change serial cross-part commit.
The S41 quiescence checks passed 15/15 verdicts, forced GC reduced residual `unreachable` to zero in one round, detailed `ca-fsck` reported `dangling = 0`, and peak `MemoryResident` was 1.99 GB.
After stage 1, stage 2's remaining cross-part target is serial `commitPart` dispatch, while CAS-only dedup HEAD and unconditional promote-manifest GET remain a separate roughly 12%-of-wall backlog.

A pre-existing ref-writer test could spin forever because its polling loop waited for a pending item that the throwing pre-carve hook had already erased; pinning execution to one CPU reproduced the hang 8/8 times while an idle 32-core machine passed 10/10.

The `RefWriterRecoverySeal.EmptyDeadRegionCarveOutStillReportsSameProcessNamespace` red was caused by a fixture combining no durable epoch, an empty data subtree, and a present mount object, a state production normally avoids because `allocateWriterEpoch` precedes mount publication.

In `build_debug`, `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` causes an allocation to throw rather than abort because `DEBUG_OR_SANITIZER_BUILD` is not defined; allocation-negative tests must distinguish `EXPECT_ANY_THROW` from `EXPECT_DEATH` by build mode.

The A1 benchmark gate kept the production-shaped `BM_FlushInstallUniqueOwner` within baseline: at N=100,000 it measured 13,355 ns before A1 and 12,428 ns after A1, while the shared-base `BM_FlushInstall` measured 21,208,894 ns after A1.
The A1 benchmark's `BM_ScratchCopy` remained O(1) at about 58 ns after the restructure, and `BM_ApplyRefLogTxn` remained within measurement noise at 770–831 ns versus 800–864 ns baseline.

The 4-hour soak harness initially classified the mount-fenced error `INVALID_STATE` code 668 as a hard failure even though its message says to retry after the disk recovers to Live; the classifier had recognized only `ABORTED` plus substrings.

A post-run observation found 56 blobs that `ca-fsck` classified as `AwaitingGc` with `dangling=0`, while GC repeatedly reported zero candidates and never drained them; fsck saw no live manifest edge but GC's in-degree view still assigned positive protection.
The 56 retained blobs were traced to four `tmp-fetch_*` refs published and dropped within one 43 ms window; their `+1` was folded about three minutes after the drop and no `-1` was recorded.

The GC scenario harness once queried the removed `min_ack` column, converted the resulting `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` into an empty list, and thereby made every GC verdict vacuously true until the observation error path was fixed.

The fsck `stale_edge` class is detail-mode only and should be emitted when every in-degree edge for a blob names an absent manifest; a blob remains ordinary `AwaitingGc` when any edge still names a present manifest.
An unmatched remove delta is currently a silent no-op at the edge reducer, so the instrumentation round added an unmatched-remove counter rather than changing the reducer's semantics.
Deferred GC rounds previously logged as `round 0` because the defer path returned before assigning `report.round`, making skipped rounds indistinguishable from empty folds.

The remaining Part B coverage gap includes gate-0 cases for `Deleting`, absent parts, other-disk matches, `Deleting → Outdated` rollback, and same-name `MOVE ... TO DISK`; the integration battery that was declared to own these cases covered none of them.

The remaining confirm test gaps include recovery that omitted one `LIST` record, an ambiguous append during abort cleanup, zero or multiple routing matches, source remount between offer and confirm, and HTTP-level transport failure or absent answers.
The older `test_replicated_fetch_by_relink` test was green for the wrong reason because its flat `count_blobs()` assertion cannot distinguish relink from a deduplicating byte fetch.

A residual post-commit exception window remains around `eraseView` and `ContentAddressedTransaction::publishStaging`'s `out_slot`: fallible work can occur after a durable commit is made but before the commit is recorded in the caller's slot.

The stage-1 A1 refinement costs one cheap COW copy per ref-log chunk and deliberately keeps the existing post-install in-place O(overlay) fold path; materializing the candidate before the PUT would create an O(n)-per-chunk regression.
